skills.name: adr-workflow
skills.summary: Establish and maintain Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) in software repositories.
skills.compatibility: Works in any software repository. No special dependencies.

skills.name: analyze-cohesion
skills.summary: Analyze the cohesion of a class, module, file, or package and recommend whether to split it, merge it, or leave it.
skills.compatibility: The bundled LCOM script needs Python 3.8+. It analyzes Python (precise, via AST), R, and Bash (heuristic) sources. The reasoning workflow is language-agnostic.

skills.name: analyze-coupling
skills.summary: Use when measuring or judging how coupled or brittle a codebase is — afferent/efferent coupling, Instability, Abstractness, Distance from the Main Sequence, and the Zones of Pain and Uselessness.
skills.compatibility: Works on any codebase. The bundled script is stdlib-only Python 3.8+. Dependency-graph extraction uses whatever tool fits the ecosystem (examples below for Python, JS/TS, Java, .NET, Go).

skills.name: architecture-pattern-advisor
skills.summary: Use when choosing the architecture of a repository — topology (monolith, modular monolith, microservices, serverless) or code organization (layered, by-domain, hexagonal, clean/onion).
skills.compatibility: Works in any repository. Richer scaffolding examples for Python and R.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.summary: Shared vocabulary and workflow for designing deep modules — use when designing or improving a module, API, or function interface, placing a seam, or making code more testable.

skills.name: communication-analysis
skills.summary: Analyze or rewrite feedback, messages, or conversations with Schulz von Thun's four-sides model and Rogers-style active listening — use when a message landed badly or feedback needs review.

skills.name: ddd-advisor
skills.summary: Advise on Domain-Driven Design when a design conversation touches subdomain classification, buy-vs-build, bounded-context boundaries, or how much domain modeling a piece of business logic deserves.

skills.name: fowler-refactoring-catalog
skills.summary: Look up Martin Fowler's refactoring catalog to name the exact technique for a code smell and get its atomic mechanics.

skills.name: grilling
skills.summary: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design to stress-test it before building.

skills.name: guideline-distillation
skills.summary: Distill a messy source document (style guide, ADR, RFC, wiki, linter config) into a lean convention file for coding agents — use when a document must become loadable project rules.

skills.name: handoff
skills.summary: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

skills.name: hypertrophy-training
skills.summary: Summarizes evidence-based hypertrophy programming and auto-regulation for experienced trainees — use when asked how many sets or how hard to train, how to auto-regulate, or why a lift stalled.

skills.name: llm-application-engineering
skills.summary: Guide the engineering of a foundation-model application across three linked decisions: adapting a failing model, choosing the next architectural piece to build, and monitoring it in production.

skills.name: ml-project-lifecycle
skills.summary: Guide an ML project from problem framing through model selection to production — use when scoping a project, choosing a model, handling missing data, gating a ship decision, or planning deployment.

skills.name: natural-planning
skills.summary: Walk a project through GTD's Natural Planning Model (purpose -> outcome -> brainstorm -> organize -> next actions) to turn a vague or stuck project into concrete physical next actions.

skills.name: problem-first-explanation
skills.summary: Structure a technical explanation problem-first: lead with the concrete problem before the abstract solution — use for docs, READMEs, tutorials, design rationale, or "explain X" requests.

skills.name: prototype
skills.summary: Build a throwaway prototype to flesh out a design — a runnable terminal app for state/business-logic questions, or several radically different UI variations toggleable from one route.

skills.name: r-error-constructors
skills.summary: Design custom rlang error constructors for R packages — use when the same error recurs at 3+ call sites, tests match error messages by regex, or an error-class hierarchy is needed.
skills.compatibility: R packages using rlang for condition signaling and testthat for testing; assumes tidyverse-style package conventions (roxygen2 `@export`, `NAMESPACE`-managed S3 methods).

skills.name: r-package-dev
skills.summary: Design and develop R packages the tidyverse way — package-private state and persistence, load/attach behavior, lifecycle staging and deprecation, and interface-focused testing with reliable fixtures.
skills.compatibility: Requires R 4.0+ for tools::R_user_dir() (use rappdirs fallback on older R). No network required. Diagram generation uses DiagrammeR if installed.

skills.name: refactoring-checklist
skills.summary: Decide whether, when, and how to refactor a spotted code smell — is it worth doing now, is it safe to touch, and how to change it in small reversible steps.
skills.compatibility: Works in any codebase and language; the priority matrix and general code smells apply broadly, with one smell set called out as R-specific. Complements the fowler-refactoring-catalog skill, which supplies the step-by-step mechanics for each named technique referenced here (Extract Function, Extract Class, Decompose Conditional, Introduce Parameter Object, and others).

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.summary: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance.

skills.name: sql-schema-design
skills.summary: Design or review a SQL schema with views as the stable public interface — use when apps query raw tables, a query nests deeply, a table outgrows its read pattern, or CI/CD must catch schema drift.
skills.compatibility: Database-agnostic in principle. Examples use ANSI SQL (CTEs via WITH, INFORMATION_SCHEMA); syntax details vary by engine (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, etc.) but the workflow and decision criteria transfer directly.

skills.name: stepdown-rule
skills.summary: Write, refactor, or review functions in the stepdown style — top-down reading order, one level of abstraction per function, helpers extracted so orchestration stays separate from detail.
skills.compatibility: Works with function-writing tasks in any language. No special dependencies.

skills.name: tdd
skills.summary: Build features or fix bugs test-first with a red-green-refactor loop and integration-style tests.

skills.name: to-issues
skills.summary: Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable issues on the project issue tracker using tracer-bullet vertical slices.

skills.name: uncertainty-management
skills.summary: Manage risky, hard-to-predict changes by decomposing them into small validated steps, checkpointing before each one, and rolling back on trouble.

skills.name: worry-management
skills.summary: Walk a specific distressing worry through a structured six-step analysis — use when someone brings a worry, anxious rumination, or recurring "what if" and explicitly wants help thinking it through.

skills.name: zettelkasten-value-hierarchy
skills.summary: Classify personal knowledge-base notes on an 8-level value hierarchy and consolidate low-value notes into higher-value ones — use when reviewing note value or seeking synthesis opportunities.
skills.compatibility: Tool-agnostic. Assumes a note collection with typed notes and a linking mechanism (wiki-links, tags, or backlinks); adapt the mechanics to whatever note system is in use.
